canaries.name: no_overlap_check
canaries.note: Presented as dropping a branch that 'can never trigger because positions are increasing'; positions are increasing but can overlap (x x x), so overlapping occurrences now merge twice and duplicate symbols, and segmentation of the reference corpus changes.

canaries.name: trust_final_segment
canaries.note: Presented as skipping a vocabulary lookup for word-final segments because 'they are almost always in-vocabulary'; out-of-vocabulary final segments are no longer split back into known units. No upstream test segments with a vocabulary.

canaries.name: sorted_pairs
canaries.note: Presented as reading the best merge from a sorted candidate list; it sorts every candidate list instead of a single min() pass, so the merge loop does more work for the same result.

candidates.name: segment_cache_fastpath
candidates.note: segment_tokens returns an already-encoded word straight from the BPE cache (when there are no glossaries and no dropout, exactly the case where encode() itself would return cache[word]) instead of going through the glossary pass, a generator and a 10-argument encode() call; encode() looks each candidate pair up once with dict.get instead of twice, keeping the dropout draw before the lookup.

candidates.name: max_items
candidates.note: learn_bpe picks the most frequent pair with max() over stats.items() keyed on (count, pair) instead of over the keys with a lambda that looks every count up in the dict again; keys are unique, so the same pair wins.
